title: Soft Body Wrecking Ball Building Demolition
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D soft-body wrecking ball building demolition scene using Three.js. No external assets or libraries beyond Three.js (via CDN) are allowed. Implement a custom soft-body / deformable physics simulation without Ammo.js or Cannon.js.

## Scene Setup
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (30, 20, 30) looking at origin. OrbitControls for mouse rotation/zoom.
- Lighting: One DirectionalLight (intensity 1.2, position 20,30,10 casting shadows), one AmbientLight (intensity 0.4), one HemisphereLight (sky 0x87CEEB, ground 0x444444, intensity 0.3).
- Ground: A large flat plane (100x100) at y=0 with a gray material, receives shadows.
- Sky: Set renderer clear color to 0x87CEEB.

## Building (Destructible)
- Construct a building from a grid of small box blocks (each block ~1x1x1 unit). The building should be 5 blocks wide, 5 blocks deep, and 8 blocks tall, centered near the origin.
- Each block is a separate Mesh with MeshStandardMaterial (color 0xCC8844 for odd rows, 0xBB7733 for even rows, like bricks).
- Each block has physics state: position, velocity, angularVelocity, mass=1, isStatic (initially true until hit), health=100.
- When a block's health drops to 0, it becomes a debris particle (scale down, change color to darker, mark destroyed).
- Blocks support each other: if a block below is destroyed, blocks above lose their static flag and begin falling under gravity.

## Wrecking Ball (Soft Body)
- A sphere of radius 2.5 composed of a soft-body mesh: generate an icosphere (subdivision 3) and treat each vertex as a mass-spring particle.
- Each vertex-particle has mass=0.5, position, velocity. Connect adjacent vertices with spring constraints (stiffness=800, damping=15, rest length = initial edge length).
- Also add internal pressure force that pushes vertices outward from the centroid to maintain volume (pressure coefficient = 50).
- The wrecking ball hangs from a crane arm. The crane arm is a visual box (1x20x1) positioned at (-15, 10, 0) colored 0xFFCC00. A cable (thin cylinder or line) connects the top of the crane to the wrecking ball center of mass.
- The cable acts as a distance constraint (max length 15) from crane tip at (-15, 20, 0).
- Wrecking ball initial position: (-15, 5, 0). Color: 0x333333 (dark iron).

## Physics Simulation
- Custom Verlet or semi-implicit Euler integration at fixed timestep (1/60).
- Gravity: (0, -9.81, 0) applied to all dynamic particles and freed blocks.
- Spring forces between soft-body vertices: F = -k*(currentLen - restLen)*direction - damping*relativeVelocity.
- Internal pressure: compute volume of soft body mesh, apply outward normal force proportional to (targetVolume - currentVolume) * pressureCoeff on each face vertex.
- Collision: sphere-box collision between wrecking ball particles and building blocks. On collision, apply impulse to both, reduce block health by impact magnitude * 5.
- Block-ground collision: blocks cannot go below y=0.
- Track total kinetic energy and total momentum for conservation monitoring.

## User Interactions
- SWING BUTTON (DOM button #swingBtn): Applies an impulse of (40, 0, 0) to all wrecking ball particles, swinging it toward the building. Each click adds impulse.
- RESET BUTTON (DOM button #resetBtn): Resets entire scene to initial state (building rebuilt, ball back to start, all counters reset).
- Keyboard 'G' toggles gravity on/off (default on). Display gravity state in HUD.
- Keyboard 'P' pauses/resumes simulation. Display pause state in HUD.
- Keyboard 'R' triggers a reverse-time replay: store last 180 frames of state, play them backward over 3 seconds, then resume. This acts as an undo.
- Keyboard ArrowUp/ArrowDown: adjust spring stiffness by ±50 (clamp 200-2000). Display in HUD.
- Click on any building block (raycaster on canvas click while holding Shift): manually destroy that block (set health=0).

## HUD / UI
- Top-left overlay div with:
  - 'Blocks Remaining: X / 200' (total = 5*5*8=200)
  - 'Blocks Destroyed: Y'
  - 'Ball Velocity: Z.ZZ m/s' (magnitude of centroid velocity)
  - 'Spring Stiffness: K'
  - 'Gravity: ON/OFF'
  - 'Paused: YES/NO'
  - 'Kinetic Energy: E.EE'
  - 'Replay Mode: YES/NO'
- Two buttons below HUD: 'Swing Wrecking Ball' (#swingBtn) and 'Reset Scene' (#resetBtn).

## State Management (CRITICAL)
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ object updated every frame with:
  - blocksTotal: 200 (constant)
  - blocksRemaining: number of non-destroyed blocks
  - blocksDestroyed: number of destroyed blocks
  - ballCentroid: {x, y, z} center of mass of wrecking ball
  - ballVelocity: {x, y, z} average velocity of ball particles
  - ballSpeed: magnitude of ballVelocity
  - springStiffness: current spring stiffness value
  - gravityEnabled: boolean
  - paused: boolean
  - kineticEnergy: total kinetic energy of system (0.5*m*v^2 summed)
  - simulationTime: elapsed simulation seconds
  - frameCount: number of physics frames computed
  - replayMode: boolean (true during reverse replay)
  - ballVolume: current soft body volume
  - initialBallVolume: volume at start
  - volumeRatio: ballVolume / initialBallVolume
  - cableLength: current distance from crane tip to ball centroid
  - maxCableLength: 15
  - cableTaut: boolean (cableLength >= maxCableLength - 0.1)
  - totalMomentumY: sum of all m*vy for dynamic objects
  - blockHealthArray: array of health values for all 200 blocks
  - swingCount: number of times swing button pressed
  - lastImpactForce: magnitude of last collision impulse
  - sceneInitialized: true when scene is ready
physics_constraints: Gravity 9.81 m/s² downward. Mass-spring soft body with configurable stiffness (200-2000), damping=15. Internal pressure maintains approximate volume (ratio should stay 0.5-1.5 under normal conditions). Cable constraint max length 15 units. Block health system: 100 HP per block, impact damage = impulse_magnitude * 5. Blocks above destroyed blocks become dynamic. Ground plane at y=0 is impenetrable. Energy should be tracked (kinetic energy). Momentum in Y should reflect gravity accumulation. No NaN values permitted in any state field.
